info.title: Crumble API
info.description: Shared HTTP contract for Crumble clients. Provider availability and cross-field business rules are validated at runtime.

BearerAuth.description: Better Auth session token from /api/auth/sign-in/email. The legacy server token is not accepted.

SessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
SessionCookie.description: Better Auth session cookie. HTTPS deployments use the __Secure- prefix. Cookie-authenticated writes require the configured Origin.

origin.description: What the bot answered: owner (a message from the owner), task (a scheduled task), script (a script task's result), bot (another bot's request), group (a group chat turn), or coding or desktop (a job's report; jobName names the job). Clients may receive other values later.

jobName.description: The job whose report the bot answered, for origin coding or desktop. A desktop job's report often asks for the owner; clients may open the bot desktop.

groupId.description: Set when a bot answered in a group chat; open the group rather than the bot chat.

waitingFor.description: Set when the bot waits for the owner's answer: approval (a desktop job action held by an intent check), credential, or login (a request the owner saves or declines). Clients may receive other values later.

LearnedEvent.description: A bot's review of one of its turns changed its skills or memory, sent as the `learned` event on /v1/events. Clients show a short notice in the bot chat and link to the change record.

coding.description: Whether bots can be given the coding tool on this server.

desktop.description: Whether bots can be given the desktop tool, and with it a bot desktop, on this server.

jobKinds.description: The kinds of background job bots can be given on this server, such as `coding` and `desktop`.

judgeModel.description: The owner's classifier; null uses the default, GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI Decisions.

choices.description: The classifier models the account's provider keys reach.

JudgeChoice.description: The model that judges now: a classifier, or a small chat model when no key reaches one. Null when no model is available; then only commit points are held.

tools.description: The bot's tools; always includes `schedule` and `codemode`.

sharedMemory.description: True whenever `tools` includes `memory`; the server ignores it in input.

delegates.description: Every other bot; with `delegate` in `tools` this bot may message any of them. The server ignores it in input.

desktopModel.description: The model for this bot's desktop jobs; unset, they use the bot's own model.

review.description: How the bot reviews its turns to learn: whether at all, after how many tool-activity rounds for skills and memory, and how much of a turn a review reads. Unset means enabled with thresholds of 10.

reviewModel.description: The model that runs this bot's reviews; unset, they use the bot's own model.

live.description: Pi Durable live progress state. In-flight assistant message content is omitted.

blocks.description: Provider content blocks, with inline image bytes removed.

heldAction.description: On a `held-action` event: the desktop job action waiting for the owner. Its state is under `/v1/agents/{id}/held-actions`.

toolDetails.description: Provider-specific tool details, including nested code-mode calls.

sources.description: In a group chat, the pages the sending bot searched or read in the turn that wrote the message.

kind.description: Where the message came from: owner, task, script (a script task's result), credential, bot, or group. Clients may receive other values later.

via.description: On an owner message sent through a message gateway: the gateway's ID, such as `discord`.

usage.description: Pi Durable usage document of the job's own conversation: tokens and cost per model and tool. Absent before its first request.
Pi Durable usage document of the job's own conversation: tokens and cost per model and tool. Absent before its first request.

holder.description: Who operates the bot desktop. While the owner holds control, the bot's desktop job pauses and only the owner's viewer input reaches the bot desktop.

changes.description: How often control changed hands. A desktop job refuses actions it planned before a change.

running.description: Whether the bot's machine runs its bot desktop now, so a passive viewer can connect. Always false for a bot without a bot desktop.

path.description: Server-relative URL of the viewer page, a noVNC client of the bot desktop. Load it in a web view; it works once and expires at expiresAt unless its connection has started by then.

memberIds.description: Member bots in the order they joined.

paused.description: Bot-started turns used up the turn budget; the owner's next message resumes the group.

botTurns.description: Bot-started turns since the owner's last message.

error.description: Why the member's latest turn failed.

passwordManager.description: The password manager the value is read from; null for a value stored in Crumble.

reference.description: Where in `passwordManager` the value is read from.

lastError.description: Why the newest use couldn't read the value from its password manager; null when it could.

instructions.default: You are a thoughtful, capable personal assistant.

error.description: Why the value couldn't be read from its password manager; the request was never sent.

fields.description: Where each field's value is read from. A login always has a username and a password; `one_time_code` only when it has one.

lastError.description: Why the newest fill couldn't read its value; null when it could.

passwordManager.description: The password manager the value is read from; null for a value stored in Crumble.

reference.description: Where in `passwordManager` the value is read from.

oneTimeCode.description: Whether the bot says the site asks for a one-time code.

error.description: Why the value couldn't be read; nothing was typed.

page.description: The URL of the page the job read last.

ownerMessages.description: The owner messages the action was checked against.

reason.description: Why the intent check held it.

name.description: The task, bot, or group chat, as named when the memory was saved.

MemorySource.description: Where the memory was saved: the owner's bot chat, the owner directly, a scheduled task, another bot's request, or a group chat.

output.description: The last 64 KiB and 2000 lines of combined output.

droppedBytes.description: Bytes dropped from the output tail.

passwordManager.description: The password manager the saved API key is read from; null for a credential stored in Crumble.

reference.description: Where in `passwordManager` the API key is read from.

thinkingLevels.description: The thinking levels this model takes, from lowest to highest. A bot's level outside them runs at the nearest one.

usedBy.description: Secrets that read their value from this password manager; it can't be disconnected while any remain.

name.description: The credential's or login's name, for `botCredential` and `botLogin`.

key.description: For `secret`, such as `mcp:<server ID>` for an MCP server token.

contributes.description: What the plugin adds to the server, so a client can show its settings where those are chosen.

kind.description: A secret is written once and never returned.

whenMissing.description: The status to show while the setting has no value.

passwordManager.description: The password manager the value is read from; null for a value stored in Crumble or no value.

reference.description: Where in `passwordManager` the value is read from.

error.description: Why the server's tools were left out of a bot's last turn, such as a missing sign-in; null once it connects again.

hasOAuthClientSecret.description: Whether the OAuth app's client secret is stored; it is never returned.

oauthClientId.description: The client ID of an OAuth app the owner registered with the server's authorization server, used instead of registering Crumble.

tokenPasswordManager.description: The password manager the token is read from; null for a token stored in Crumble or no token.

tokenReference.description: Where in `tokenPasswordManager` the token is read from.

post.description: Issue a single-use viewer link for the bot desktop. The page and its WebSocket live outside /v1 and need no Authorization header: the link is the credential. With passive=true the link is watch-only: it neither boots the bot's machine nor keeps it awake, and its connection ends when the machine stops. 409 when the bot has no bot desktop.

get.description: Server-sent events. Each activity event carries a ReplyEvent or ChatPreviewEvent JSON object in data. Each learned event carries a LearnedEvent: what a bot's review of one turn changed; GET /v1/agents/{id}/reviews lists them durably. Current chat previews replay on connection; finished replies and learned events are not replayed. Heartbeat events carry {} every 15 seconds. Authenticate with the Authorization header. No Last-Event-ID replay.
